headline: Demand strength lifts profits, margins, and guidance
summary_short: Rockwell Automation reported fiscal Q3 2026 (our FY2026 Q2) revenue of $2.31B, up 7.9% y/y and 3.3% q/q, as diluted EPS rose 40.4% y/y to $3.65 on margin expansion; the company also raised its full-year sales-growth and EPS guidance.
summary_long: Revenue was $2.31B, up 7.9% y/y and 3.3% q/q, with organic sales up 10% on strength in semiconductor, data center, and warehouse automation, plus improving automotive and life sciences; divestitures (Sensia JV dissolution) cut sales 3%. Operating margin expanded to 23.8% (+2.6ppt y/y) and net margin to 17.6% (+3.9ppt y/y) on higher volume, favorable mix, and a Sensia-dissolution margin benefit, partly offset by negative price/cost. Net income rose 38.3% y/y to $408M; diluted EPS rose 40.4% y/y to $3.65. Free cash flow was $654M. Rockwell raised FY2026 guidance: sales growth to 7.5%-9.5% (from 5%-9%) and diluted EPS to $12.72-$13.02 (from $11.88-$12.48).

drivers.explanation: Organic sales rose 10% on strength in semiconductor, data center, and warehouse automation plus improving automotive and life sciences demand; divestitures (Sensia dissolution) cut sales 3%, FX added 1%.
Pre-tax and Enterprise operating margin expansion driven by higher sales volume, favorable mix, and the Sensia joint-venture dissolution margin benefit, partly offset by negative price/cost.
Net income and diluted EPS growth were primarily due to higher pre-tax margin; Adjusted EPS growth was primarily due to higher Enterprise operating margin.
Tracks net income growth; weighted diluted shares fell 1.2% y/y on buybacks, a small additional lift to per-share EPS.

CEO cited healthy customer demand, accelerated innovation, and disciplined execution; Software & Control led segment growth (organic +18%) and Intelligent Devices grew organic +10%, while Lifecycle Services organic sales fell 2% on lower project volume.
